title: InvoiceSchemaUpgrade backfill is idempotent, chunked, and touches nothing but due_date
steps: Read InvoiceSchemaUpgrade.java (not executed against a populated database, per the brief)
expected: Re-runnable no-op after the first pass; only due_date and payment_term written; status/paid_amount untouched; the column is then made NOT NULL; failure is non-fatal because Invoice#onCreate is a last resort
actual: All eight properties hold in the source: keyset-paged select of due_date-null rows in 1000-row chunks; the UPDATE re-checks due_date is null so a second run writes zero rows; only due_date and payment_term appear in the SET clause; the due date is computed as InvoiceDates.dayOf(invoiceDate)+term days in Java (UTC) rather than by the database, so H2's session zone cannot date a late-evening invoice a day out; the audit entry is written only when filled > 0, so a restart does not re-file it; the column is then altered to NOT NULL (Postgres/H2 only, skipped when already not null); and any SQLException is logged as a warning because Invoice#onCreate (Invoice.java:99) independently defaults a missing due date.
evidence: ok: selects only undated rows | ok: update guarded by due_date is null (re-run is a no-op) | ok: writes only due_date and payment_term | ok: chunked with a keyset cursor | ok: computes the day in Java (UTC), not in SQL | ok: audits only when rows moved | ok: makes due_date NOT NULL afterwards | ok: SQL failure is a warning, not fatal

GET /api/audit?entityType=INVOICE&entityId=0 answers HTTP 200 (the id belongs to no invoice, so the row is unreachable through the History tab by design). title: DOCUMENT_VIEW and DOCUMENT_MANAGE are seeded idempotently — re-running duplicates nothing and drops nothing
steps: Read DataSeeder.run and its three helpers, then checked the live database through GET /api/privileges and GET /api/roles.
expected: One privilege row per name on any number of boots; no role gaining a duplicate entry; no grant silently dropped.
actual: Privilege rows are created through findByName().orElseGet(save) (DataSeeder:57-63), so a re-run finds each of DOCUMENT_VIEW / DOCUMENT_MANAGE and creates nothing — observed exactly one row for each. Built-in roles go through upsertRole, which assigns a Set (DataSeeder:187-193) — re-running rewrites the same set, so no duplicates and no loss for ADMIN/CASHIER/VIEWER. POC roles go through createRoleIfAbsent (DataSeeder:200-217), which on a second boot adds only privileges in createdNow (empty on a re-run) and skips any the role already holds — so nothing is added twice and nothing is removed. DOCUMENT_MANAGE on CUSTOMER goes through keptOrNew (DataSeeder:108, 225-234): on a re-run createdNow is empty and the privilege is kept because the role already holds it, so the grant survives; an operator's revocation would also survive, which is the stated intent (impl doc §4.5). Observed live: exactly one DOCUMENT_VIEW row and one DOCUMENT_MANAGE row, no duplicate entry in any of the 7 seeded roles' privilege lists, and grants matching the code exactly.

title: The implementation doc says POC document access is limited to 'their POC book'; two of the three POC roles are not book-limited at all
steps: custB / invB / payB carry no POC seat and no ownership for the three probe POC users (verified through GET /api/customers/{custB}/pocs and the records' own POC fields). Each POC role then listed, downloaded and uploaded documents on those foreign records.

CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC and COLLECTION_POC both got 200 on GET /api/customers/{custB}, /api/invoices/{invB} and /api/payments/{payB}, 200 on the document list and 200 on downloading an INTERNAL document on each of those foreign records — and CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC uploaded to custB (201, then deleted it 204), COLLECTION_POC uploaded to payB (201, 204). Cause: both roles are seeded with SCOPE_OVERRIDE (DataSeeder.java:138 and :153), which by design lifts the book restriction; their ageing Coverage is correspondingly ALL, not BOOK.
